_meta.horse: native Japanese horse (Kiso / Misaki / Taishū type), 1.35 m at the withers, ~330 kg; hip joint 0.98 m, shoulder joint 1.00 m above the ground
_meta.scaling: dynamic similarity (Alexander & Jayes 1983): at equal Froude number Fr = v²/(g·h_hip) angles, fractions, duty factors and lengths/h are equal; lengths ×(h/h_ref), times ×√(h/h_ref), speeds ×√(h/h_ref). 4.0 m/s → Fr 1.66 (= a Warmblood with a 1.20 m hip at 4.4 m/s, Clayton's 1994 medium trot; = an Icelandic horse of 1.41 m at 4.1 m/s); 3.2 m/s → Fr 1.07; 5.0 m/s → Fr 2.60
_meta.conventions: angles between the origins of the rig's bones (definitions in docs/trot-lab.md): compare excursions and changes relative to the square stand, not absolute values; notes give the source (author, year) of each literature-derived range, and the 'engineering tolerance' entries are limits of the instrument, not literature values

stride.freq_hz.note: Clayton 1994 medium trot (Fr 1.67): 1.37 Hz at h 1.22 m → 1.53 Hz scaled; ridden Icelandic horses at Fr ~1.7 (Rhodin 2022, stride 0.59 s) → 1.73 Hz; Alexander & Jayes λ/h = 2.3·Fr^0.3 → 1.52 Hz. Ponies: a higher stride frequency than Warmbloods

stride.length_m.note: v/f with the frequency above: 4.0/1.80…4.0/1.45; Alexander & Jayes 1983 → 2.62 m; Icelandic horses ~2.3 m at equal Fr

duty.fore.note: trot: 0.35–0.42 in collected trot (Clayton & Hobbs 2019, from Clayton 1997 and Holmström 1994); 0.46–0.49 in hand trot with IMUs (Rhodin 2022: WB 0.49, Iberian 0.49, Icelandic 0.46); duty factor falls with speed (Weishaupt 2010). Fore ≥ hind at the trot (Rhodin 2022; Biknevicius 2006)

duty.hind.note: Rhodin 2022: hind 0.39 (WB), 0.43 (Iberian), 0.42–0.46 (Icelandic); as a rule a little below the fore at the trot

suspension.frac.note: total of the two suspensions: 2–4 % in hand at low speed (Rhodin 2022), 76 ms per phase in high-level collected trot (Clayton 1997 via Clayton & Hobbs 2019), plateau ~90 ms per phase at the higher speeds (Weishaupt 2010); at Fr 1.66 ~5–20 % expected

suspension.count.note: two suspensions per stride (one after each diagonal) at Fr > ~1 (Clayton & Hobbs 2019)

diag.dap_td_ms.note: dissociation at touchdown (DAP): +29.8 ± 7.6 ms in quality SWB stallions (Holmström 1994); in hand trot WB −2.6 % of the stride ≈ −20 ms, Iberian −1.2 % (Rhodin 2022); with speed it tends toward hind first (Hobbs, Bertram & Clayton 2016). Kiso / Misaki / Taishū lack the DMRT3 allele for ambling gaits (Chandra Paul 2020) → a diagonal trot, not the −4.8 % of Icelandic horses

diag.dap_td_ms.LF_RH.note: as diag.dap_td_ms, single diagonal (variability between diagonals: Hobbs 2016)

diag.dap_lo_ms.note: 'lift-off is almost always hind first' (Clayton & Hobbs 2019); estimate: dap_td + (fore stance − hind stance), with fore stances 0–70 ms longer (Rhodin 2022) → ~0…+50 ms

contact.slip_mm.fore.note: engineering tolerance: the impact slip (1–4 cm, ~20 ms: Holden-Douilly 2013 at 7 m/s on sand; Pardoe 2001) falls in the excluded first 10 %; after that the hoof is stationary until the heel lifts on hard ground (Clayton, Mechanics of equine locomotion). Consistent with the 8 / 20 mm limits

contact.slip_full_mm.note: whole contact: impact slip (≤ 2–3 cm on hard ground) + displacement of the sole centre as the hoof rotates about the toe (r·(1−cos θ), r ≈ 57 mm: ~15–30 mm at 45–60°)

contact.scrape_mm.note: a sound horse does not scrape its hooves at the trot (toe dragging is a clinical sign); measurement tolerance

contact.penetration_mm.note: the game's ground is rigid: the hoof must not enter it; engineering tolerance (hard limit 10 mm)

contact.float_mm.note: at mid-stance the sole is on the ground; ±2 mm of measurement tolerance

contact.td_hvel_mps.fore.note: ground speed matching: long late-swing retraction in the forelimbs (~22 % of the stride: Holmström 1994, Clayton & Hobbs 2019); on the treadmill at 4.4 m/s the fore hoof lands at −2.5 ± 0.7 m/s in the laboratory frame ≈ +1.9 m/s relative to the belt (Reiser et al. 2005, converted here); ×0.9 for the size, mean over the last 1/60 s

contact.td_hvel_mps.hind.note: short hind retraction (~5 % of the stride): horizontal velocity at impact greater than in the fore (Back et al. 1995 AJVR; Clayton & Hobbs 2019) but always below the trunk speed (the hoof is already retracting)

contact.td_vvel_mps.fore.note: Reiser et al. 2005: −1.9 ± 0.5 m/s at the trot at 4.4 m/s; ×0.9 for the size; vertical velocity fore > hind (Back et al. 1995 AJVR)

contact.td_vvel_mps.hind.note: lower than in the fore (Back et al. 1995 AJVR); wide range, no direct value

contact.td_pitch_deg.fore.note: sound horses on hard ground: heel-first or flat landing, toe-first is atypical (Clayton 1990; Gorissen 2018: adults prefer a heel-first or lateral-first landing)

contact.breakover_toe_slip_mm.note: in breakover the hoof rotates about the stationary toe (Clayton, Mechanics of equine locomotion); a few mm of twist / slip

contact.breakover_at.fore.note: breakover 70–77 ms of a ~330 ms stance (Gottleib et al. 2025, hoof-mounted IMU, asphalt) → heel up at ~0.78 of the contact; 1 = flat lift-off, which a real horse does not do

contact.breakover_at.hind.note: as contact.breakover_at.fore (no direct hind data: same digit mechanics)

trunk.withers_dy_mm.note: withers peak-to-peak: WB 86–94 mm (5–95 %: 66–106; Hardeman 2020) and 92 mm (Rhodin 2022) ×0.82 → 54–87; Icelandic 47 mm (Rhodin 2022); spring-mass estimate for duty 0.36–0.44 at 1.5 Hz: 46–65 mm

trunk.sacrum_dy_mm.note: sacrum (croup): WB 90–96 mm (5–95 %: 77–106; Hardeman 2020), 89 mm (Rhodin 2022) ×0.82 → 63–87; Icelandic 56 mm; trunk COM 86 ± 18 mm at 4.4 m/s in ridden Lusitanos (Hobbs & Clayton 2019) ×0.82 → 71

trunk.body_dy_mm.note: trunk centre: BCM (body centre of mass) 53 ± 6 mm, 27 % less than the outer trunk (Buchner 2000); Hobbs & Clayton 2019 as above

trunk.withers_min_at_stance.note: minima at mid-stance: withers at 39–42 % of the fore stance (medians, IQR ±4–6; Rhodin 2022); 'high at touchdown and lift-off, lowest at mid-stance' (Hobbs & Clayton 2019). Translated onto the diagonal union with DAP 0…+30 ms

trunk.sacrum_min_at_stance.note: sacrum at 37–45 % of the hind stance (Rhodin 2022)

trunk.flight_accel_mps2.note: in suspension the trunk is in free fall: −9.81 m/s²; ±20 % for the transients at the edges of the aerial phase (hard limit ±30 %)

trunk.pitch_deg.note: trunk pitch: ROM 0.9–1.4° per diagonal (Hobbs, Bertram & Clayton 2016); vertebrae 2.8–4.9° (Faber 2001, bone-mounted markers); one cycle per diagonal, i.e. two per stride (Hardeman 2020)

trunk.roll_deg.note: axial rotation of the thoracic vertebrae: 3.1–3.3° (T10, T13) up to 4.6–5.8° (others; Faber 2001, 4 m/s, bone-mounted markers)

trunk.pelvis_roll_deg.note: pelvis roll in straight-line trot: median 8.5° (5–95 %: 5.8–9.1) on a hard surface, 9.7° (6.4–12.9) on a soft one (Hardeman 2020); angles are size-invariant

trunk.lateral_mm.note: mediolateral oscillation: BCM 19 ± 4 mm, the trunk 34 % more (~29 mm) (Buchner 2000) ×0.82 → ~15–25 mm

trunk.withers_lateral_mm.note: lateral oscillation of the trunk plus the roll of the thorax (~3–5°) at ~0.5 m above the axis; estimate

head.poll_dy_mm.note: head peak-to-peak in hand trot: WB 67–71 mm (5–95 %: 52–100; Hardeman 2020), 78 mm (Rhodin 2022), Iberian 64, Icelandic 61 (in hand) and 69 (ridden); ×0.82 for the WB

head.muzzle_dy_mm.note: as the poll plus the pitch of the head

head.lag_ms.note: difference between the head and withers minima: WB −3.3 %, Iberian −1.6 %, Icelandic +1.1 % of the stride (head later: a negative value in Rhodin's 2022 convention) → ~−7…+26 ms

fore.carpus_stance_dev_deg.note: the carpus 'snaps into hyperextension' at the start of stance (Back et al. 1995a) and begins to flex at the end of stance: ROM in stance 15 ± 6° (Clayton et al. 2004, bone-mounted markers)

fore.carpus_max_flex_deg.note: carpus in swing: ROM 76 ± 13° (Clayton et al. 2004); minimum angle 99° → 81° of flexion in the Bardigiano (Martuzzi et al. 2009); grows with speed (Cruz et al. 2018)

fore.carpus_max_flex_at_swing.note: flexion begins at the end of stance and continues until mid-swing (Clayton et al. 2004)

fore.fetlock_ext_deg.note: extension beyond the standing value at mid-stance: fetlock standing ~145–150° dorsal, at mid-stance ~121° (Martuzzi et al. 2009) → ~25–30°; proportional to the vertical force (McGuigan & Wilson 2003; Clayton). The standing rig (−30.5°) is anatomical

fore.fetlock_ext_at_stance.note: maximum extension at mid-stance, with the metacarpus vertical and at peak vertical force (Clayton, Mechanics of equine locomotion); fore GRF peak at 43–48 % of stance (Hobbs, Bertram & Clayton 2016)

fore.elbow_rom_deg.note: elbow 91–146° → ROM ~54° (Martuzzi et al. 2009, Bardigiano); the elbow never reaches full extension (max ~146°)

fore.shoulder_rom_deg.note: scapulohumeral joint: ROM of a few tens of degrees (Back et al. 1995a; Morales 1998); estimate, no direct value accessible — wide range

fore.scap_rom_deg.note: pendular rotation of the scapula in sync with the limb (Back et al. 1995a); protraction–retraction of the whole limb 39.5° at 4.4 m/s (Hobbs & Clayton 2019), of which the scapula is about half; estimate

fore.carpus_rom_deg.note: Clayton 2004 (76 ± 13 in swing + hyperextension in stance); Martuzzi 2009 ~81°

fore.fetlock_rom_deg.note: fore fetlock: flexion–extension 77 ± 5° at the trot (Clayton et al. 2007, bone-mounted markers); 121–213° → ~92° (Martuzzi 2009): extension in stance + strong flexion in swing

fore.hoof_max_h_mm.note: hoof height in swing: 13–14 cm (early peak) and ~12 cm (late peak) in adult horses at ~3 m/s (Gottleib et al. 2025); ×0.82 for the size, a little more for the speed; the Japanese native horses are not high-action horses

fore.hoof_max_h_at_swing.note: the toe arc peaks shortly after lift-off, then follows a low path with a second small rise before touchdown (Clayton 1990; Clayton, Mechanics…; Gottleib 2025)

hind.hock_stance_yield_deg.note: the hock flexes during impact / loading and extends at the end of stance (Back et al. 1995b; Gnagey et al. 2006; Holmström 1994); magnitude estimated

hind.hock_max_flex_deg.note: maximum flexion in swing beyond the standing value: tarsus ROM ~54° (97–152°, Martuzzi 2009), with the end-of-stance extension close to the standing angle (150–165°, Gnagey 2006) → ~45–55° beyond standing

hind.hock_max_flex_at_swing.note: hock, stifle and fetlock flex together (reciprocal apparatus) in the first half of swing (Back et al. 1995b; Clayton)

hind.stifle_rom_deg.note: stifle 120–161° → ROM ~41° (Martuzzi 2009); coupled to the hock by the reciprocal apparatus

hind.hock_rom_deg.note: tarsus ROM ~54° (Martuzzi 2009); the hock never reaches full extension (maximum ~152–165°, Martuzzi 2009, Gnagey 2006)

hind.hip_rom_deg.note: hip 105–127° → ROM ~22° (Martuzzi 2009); protraction–retraction of the whole limb 44.6° at 4.4 m/s (Hobbs & Clayton 2019) with the contribution of the pelvis and the distal joints

hind.fetlock_ext_deg.note: the hind fetlock extends less than the fore (hind GRF peak ~8.3–9.4 N/kg against ~11 fore: Hobbs, Bertram & Clayton 2016)

hind.fetlock_ext_at_stance.note: with the hind vertical force peak, at 40–45 % of stance (Hobbs, Bertram & Clayton 2016)

hind.fetlock_rom_deg.note: hind fetlock: extension in stance and flexion in swing coupled to the hock and stifle (Back et al. 1995b); estimate

hind.hoof_max_h_mm.note: the hind hoof flies lower than the fore; estimate scaled from the fore arcs (Gottleib 2025) and from Muybridge's plates 596/601

hind.hoof_max_h_at_swing.note: peak in the first half of swing, as in the fore

track.overtrack_mm.left.note: print overlap (overtrack) ≈ λ/2 − diagonal distance: dressage medium trot (Clayton 1994, λ 3.26 m) ~0.33 m → ×0.82 ~0.27 m; short stride of ponies (Icelandic ~2.3 m) → ~0.1 m

leg.compression_pct.fore.note: fore limb compression relative to the standing length: 6.99 ± 1.77 % at 4.4 m/s, 4.46 % at 2.7 m/s (Hobbs & Clayton 2019, scapular spine → distal interphalangeal joint); here shoulder → sole relative to touchdown: a little more

leg.compression_pct.hind.note: hind 8.53 ± 2.13 % at 4.4 m/s (Hobbs & Clayton 2019, trochanter → distal interphalangeal joint); relative to touchdown +1–2 %

smooth.ik_unreached_frames.note: engineering tolerance: the limb must reach its target (internal label, not geometry)

smooth.max_bone_step_deg.note: a real fetlock or carpus reaches ~600–1000°/s in swing → ≤ 15–17° per frame at 60 Hz; beyond that is a visible jump (hard limit 25°)

smooth.max_bone_step_all_deg.note: as above, with the ears and tail

v3.2.stride.freq_hz.note: Fr 1.07: WB working trot (Clayton 1994, f̂ 0.47) and Icelandic horses in hand (f̂ 0.51), scaled

v3.2.duty.fore.note: slow trot: higher duty factor (Rhodin 2022; Weishaupt 2010)

v3.2.suspension.frac.note: at Fr ~1 the suspension is short or absent (Rhodin 2022: 2–4 % in hand)

v3.2.trunk.withers_min_at_stance.note: minimum at mid-stance at every speed (Hobbs & Clayton 2019)

v5.0.stride.freq_hz.note: Fr 2.60: extended trot (Clayton 1994, f̂ ~0.49) and faster ponies; the frequency grows little with speed

v5.0.duty.fore.note: duty factor falls with speed (Weishaupt 2010; Clayton 1994)

v5.0.suspension.frac.note: longer suspensions with speed, plateau ~90 ms per phase (Weishaupt 2010)

robust.accel.slip_mm.note: engineering tolerance under the 30 mm hard limit (transitions included)

robust.accel.penetration_mm.note: as in the trot: the hoof does not enter the ground (hard limit 15 mm)

robust.accel.max_bone_step_deg.note: maximum bone step per frame at 60 Hz (hard limit 25°); at the gallop the distal joints move faster

robust.accel.hover_mm.note: every hoof must touch the ground (above 4 mm it never does); negative values are penetration, already counted by penetration_mm

robust.accel.ik_unreached_frames.note: ≤ ~2 % of the 60 Hz frames; internal label

robust.turn_left.duty_hind.note: trot at 4.0 m/s on an 8 m circle: as the straight trot, a little wider

robust.slope_up.duty_hind.note: trot on a 15 % grade: all four hooves must land; stances similar to level ground (Dutto et al. 2004), wide range

robust.walk.duty_hind.note: walk at 1.8 m/s (Fr 0.34): fore duty factor 0.62–0.65, hind 0.57–0.59 (Rhodin 2022, three breeds), a little less in a brisk walk
